basics.name: Chris Lam
basics.label: Product Designer for AI-native products
basics.summary: Product designer, 14 years shipping healthcare, marketplace, education, and consumer software. I own the work from research through interaction design to design systems, and I ship production code (React, TypeScript, Python), so design intent survives to what users actually touch. Results: GoodRx coupon conversion from 2% to 5%, TaskRabbit NPS from about -5 to the mid-50s, and a Clover Health redesign that nurses said gave them back 1-2 hours of chart prep a day. Seeking senior product design roles on AI-native teams.

work.name: y30
work.summary: Co-founder through Jul 2026; advising since. Voice AI for older adults and their care teams.
highlights: Built an FSM safety engine where crisis paths are deterministic code, not prompt instructions, a hard state the model cannot override.
Architected a streaming speech-to-text to LLM to text-to-speech pipeline (multi-provider, deep fallback) fronted by a deterministic state machine.
Scoped the language model to phrasing and warmth while conversation flow runs as a deterministic state machine; about half of routing decisions resolve with no model call.
Built a layered quality loop: manual QA scripts, automated and adversarial checks, and live safety smoke tests. Confirmed failures became regression tests after human review.
Designed elder-first voice UX across browser voice, a tested phone path, and visual games, all around one agent.
Tested with 11 people outside the founding team, including four elder-care professionals: a facility owner-operator, two geriatric physicians, and a senior-rehabilitation specialist.

work.name: PlaySesh
work.summary: Collaborative game development tools for indie developers, built inside Discord. Started while finishing at Modus Create.
highlights: Started 0 to 1 solo, then recruited a co-founder and founding engineer; remained CEO, setting company and product direction, owning product and design, and contributing hands-on testing and implementation.
Shipped Whiteboard by PlaySesh inside Discord with TLDraw, Cloudflare Durable Objects, and R2; active development paused in March 2026 and the Discord product remains live.

Grew organically to over 6,700 authorized Discord accounts, 161 server installs, and 77 individual-user installs; peaked at 1,043 monthly active users (January 2026). Discord counts are approximate, as of September 11, 2026.

work.name: Modus Create
work.summary: Designed and implemented cross-app dark mode and visual consistency for Jira and Confluence Cloud products serving a 500K+ installed/reachable user base. Shipped through PR review, automated tests, visual QA, and the team's existing CI/CD; authored README and setup documentation.
work._gap_before: Jan-Jun 2023: deliberate time off to build production engineering depth. Not an unexplained gap; it is the pivot the whole positioning rests on.

work.name: StartPlaying
work.summary: First designer at a YC W20, a16z-backed seed-stage TTRPG marketplace. Shipped Stripe-based marketplace money flows, refunds, and player-debt reconciliation, enabling correct and timely GM payouts and traceable accounting. Completed a GM onboarding redesign that was not launched.

work.name: doc.ai (acquired by Sharecare)
work.summary: A rescue hire at doc.ai as it prepared for its acquisition by Sharecare. Became sole design owner for Omix, consolidating fragmented clinical-study workflows into a working engineering build validated with researchers; canceled before public launch after the acquisition.

work.name: Pathstream
work.summary: Operated as lead designer. First design hire at a career-development and LMS platform.
highlights: Redesigned the core lesson experience on a live platform, mid-cohort, without forcing a rewrite of 60-80 hours of existing course content.
Designed the platform's shared interface system with engineer Matthew Smith, who implemented it in React with Storybook and Chromatic on top of Ant Design.
Ran the research that set the direction: a 26-screen product audit in week three, three rounds of usability testing, five course-author co-design sessions, and instructor interviews.

Audited the interface library and found the drift: sixteen colors where four grays were all labeled Text, two different values both called Primary Button, body copy at four sizes, and a 10.3px type size shipping to adult learners.
work._unverified: Storybook confirmed by Chris 2026-08-02; the repo is Pathstream's and he has no access, which is normal for employed work. WCAG 2.1 AA still unconfirmed: the archive shows accessibility judgment (killed an icon-only progress timeline on ADA grounds, flagged a ~1.7:1 contrast failure) but no audit, conformance report, or CI gate. Ask before restoring that one.

work.name: Iodine (acquired by GoodRx)
work.summary: First full-time designer, on GoodRx's special research and experimentation team. Title was self-assigned. A contractor preceded me and never converted. GoodRx later IPO'd (NASDAQ: GDRX).
highlights: Redesigned the coupon redemption flow; conversion rate 2% to 5%.
Ran a series of conversion projects across the drug pages: 10% lift on mobile, 25% on desktop.
Designed and personally coded (JavaScript/D3) the interactive GoodRx Research data visualizations referenced in the New York Times and on Good Morning America / ABC News.
Iodine.com won the Webby for Best Health Website (2018). I was the product's designer.
Built 50-state prescription-price fact sheets with GoodRx co-CEO Doug Hirsch, used in advocacy around S.2554 and S.2553 on drug price transparency.

work.name: Clover Health
work.summary: Second designer, joined when it was about 30 people and founder-funded, months before the Series A. The title was deliberately broad. Operated as a product design lead. Clover later went public (Nasdaq: CLOV, 2021).
highlights: Helped build the design function as the second designer: established how design, engineering, and product worked together, sat in product development, and co-wrote PRDs with the product manager.
Redesigned the nurse-practitioner home-visit iPad web app end to end through contextual shadowing; nurses reported 1-2 hours of chart prep gone each day and no longer carried stacks of paper.
Led cross-functional alignment across design, engineering, product, data science, and medical.

work.name: TaskRabbit
work.summary: Worked on the 2014 rebrand; TaskRabbit later acquired by IKEA (2017).
highlights: Hired by founder and CEO Leah Busque onto a new design team as TaskRabbit moved from bidding to direct hire. Owned the Tasker side of the experience outright and contributed to the consumer side.
Tasker NPS recovered from about -5 in mid-2014 to the mid-50s; Client NPS to the high-40s.

Led the mobile design system after the 2014 rebrand: one type scale, an icon set specified at six sizes, four named colour families each with a ten-step scale, and component specs through to empty states. Picked it up because nobody owned it and the design team had drifted, with each designer owning different pieces.

work.name: Amazon
highlights: Completed the implementation-ready design for the buy-and-gift Prime flow, projected to drive 1M+ new subscribers.
Partnered with Samsung on the Amazon Prime Music app for the Samsung Shape wireless speaker.

meta.note: Seeking senior product design roles, full-time. Remote US from Honolulu (preferred), working West Coast hours. Can also work remotely from Seattle or the Bay Area. Open to relocation for the right role.
meta.locationLine: Remote US from Honolulu, HI · Or remote from Seattle / Bay Area · West Coast hours · Open to relocation
